minutes.headline: Sewer Commission moved to accept a combined sewer and generator maintenance contract with Small Water Systems
minutes.summary: The commission took up a combined Small Water Systems contract for sewer and generator maintenance, and a motion to accept it was made and seconded. It asked for a breakdown of an increase in the Flow Assessment contract. It reviewed inflow and infiltration inspection letters, engineering bids for the SRF project, and the capacity fee policy, then adjourned.

votes.motion: Accept the Small Water Systems contract for the upcoming fiscal year, covering sewer maintenance and maintenance of all generators.

budget_items.what_was_said: The new contract came in with an increase said to be within budget, combined with the generator maintenance program into one contract.
Several amounts were mentioned before the motion named a total for sewer and generator maintenance.
figures_as_heard: eighty four thousand three hundred and seventy five dollars

budget_items.what_was_said: A member asked for a breakdown and justification of the increase in the contract. Another noted the price had not been raised in four years.
Annual permit fees are due July 1; the fee differs for significantly non-compliant and compliant establishments.
Legal counsel indicated a capacity fee can be charged to new users on extensions. Whether it can continue after the Fitchburg debt is paid is unresolved.
Members discussed the already-approved amount and the original proposal plus added specifications.

decisions.decision: Commission will interview the low-bidding engineering firm for the SRF project this week.
The business manager will send a written request to Flow Assessment for a breakdown and justification of the increase.
The main inspection letter will be sent out, with other letters reviewed at a later meeting; mandatory inspection wording to cite the regulation.
Grease trap compliance and outreach to be put on the next agenda.
Troy volunteered to help with the privately funded sewer extension policy.
Members to bring goal ideas for the business manager to the next meeting.
Next meeting set for July 8th at the DPW; a Friday meeting at 1:30 on the engineering contract.

what_happened.line: A motion to accept a combined Small Water Systems contract for sewer and generator maintenance was made and seconded; the vote was not audible in the captions.
The commission asked the business manager to request a written breakdown and justification from Flow Assessment for an increase in its contract.
The commission will interview the low-bidding engineering firm for the SRF project this week.
The main inflow and infiltration inspection letter will go out, with mandatory inspection wording to cite the regulation.
Capacity fee policy was left unresolved, including whether a fee can continue after the Fitchburg debt is paid. Grease trap compliance goes on the next agenda.

why_it_matters: Sewer maintenance contracts and capacity fees feed into sewer rates and charges for new connections, so contract increases and the end of the Fitchburg debt bear on what sewer users pay.
Inspection letters and grease trap permits can place requirements and fees on property owners and restaurants.
